title: Advertised 'Internet Price' excludes mandatory-looking dealer add-ons that are added back to reach 'Selling Price'
quote:
Retail Price
$36,995
Savings
$7,000
Internet Price
$29,995
Doc Fee
$85
Z Shield
$959
SELLING PRICE
$31,039
recommendation: Two issues. (1) Advertised-price stacking: 'Internet Price' ($29,995) is presented as the price, but a non-government Doc Fee ($85) and a 'Z Shield' add-on ($959) are then added to reach 'SELLING PRICE' ($31,039). Under VC §11713.1(e) only government fees (tax/license/registration) may be excluded from the advertised price; dealer add-ons and doc fees may not be added on top of an advertised price. The vehicle cannot actually be bought at the advertised $29,995. (2) Savings substantiation: the '$7,000 Savings' is measured off 'Retail Price $36,995' — verify $36,995 is a bona fide, documented prior/market price and not an inflated reference. Fix: make the all-in price (excluding only tax and government fees) the single advertised price; if Z Shield is optional, remove it from the default price stack and label it optional; substantiate every 'Retail Price'/'Savings' figure with records. Attorney review recommended.
